subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle design: a six-wheeled carrier with a turret-mounted railgun and four deployable stabiliser outriggers, aiming for a static model without unnecessary joint complexity.

I'm working out dimensions and construction approach—roughly 9m length, wheels radius 0.65m resting on the ground, stabiliser legs with pads touching down, and building everything from boxes with helper functions plus hazard stripe textures, panelled camo paint, and glowing coil rail accents. For the wheels I'm detailing tire and hub geometry with bolts and considering tread options.

Now I'm laying out the chassis: six wheels across three axles, a sloped-windscreen cab up front, a chamfered turret toward the rear with an extruded side profile, and a twin-rail railgun angled upward about 12 degrees extending forward from the turret.

Still writing railgun details...

Still building outrigger geometry...

Placing rear legs behind the rear axle keeps everything clear of the hull. For colors I'm settling on an olive-drab camo mottle for the hull with dark gray, steel, orange accent, cyan glow, and near-black tire tones, keeping the palette compact. I'm also planning textures like hazard stripes, an emblem, a unit stencil reading "RG-06", visor glass, hub detail, vent grille, and a warning label.

Now I'm adding extra greebles: antennas, glowing headlight boxes, side ammo boxes, handrails, exhaust stacks, a lathed radar dish, sensor dome, tow hooks, mud flaps, side skirts, and ladder rungs, aiming for roughly a hundred parts total with helper functions for boxes and mirrored loops. Since this is a static model without joints, I can skip bone rigging and just paint the panels with a riveted camo texture on the hull sides.

For the camo pattern itself, I'm layering nested mottle functions with different seeds and scales, then wrapping that in a paneled texture with visible rivets for the hull surface. I'm now sketching the turret's side profile as a series of coordinate points to extrude into its final shape.

For the cab, I'm positioning a boxy front section with a sloped windscreen achieved through rotation, placing a slanted plane near the front to suggest the angled glass.

I'm computing the windscreen plane's size and normal direction, sizing it at roughly 1.9 by 0.85 with a slight lift, and planning a dark glass texture with cyan HUD lines, orienting it against the world up axis.

Now I'm working out the chassis dimensions and wheel placements—setting box height around 0.95 centered near y=1.325, length about 8.6 along z, width 2.3, with wheels positioned at x≈±1.45 so they touch the chassis sides cleanly. I'm also sizing fender boxes to sit just above the wheel tops without clipping, adjusting their y-position to clear the wheel radius with an arch side plate.

I'm positioning the cab and turret on top of the chassis at y=1.8, giving the turret a ring cylinder and box shape, then working out the railgun's trunnion mount point and rail geometry—calculating where the breech sits inside the turret and where the barrel tip extends forward and upward, checking it clears the cab roof.

I'm adjusting the pivot height and pitch angle to resolve a clearance conflict where the rails were dipping too close to the cab roof, raising the mount point so the rails sit clear above the turret roof near the mantlet.

With the barrel pitched up, the muzzle rises well above the hull, giving a total rail length around 10.6 units—reasonable for a railgun-type weapon. I'm now setting up cradle supports connecting the turret roof to the rail underside, using offset boxes plus trunnion cylinders, and defining a perpendicular "up" vector to help position rail segments along the barrel's length and width.

Still writing rail geometry...

Still placing muzzle glow tips and brake geometry, then moving to the capacitor banks along the turret sides—orange-painted cylinders with dark end caps and glow rings positioned symmetrically at the turret flanks.

For the rear, I'm adding a power generator block behind the turret with vent textures and exhaust stacks, checking the z-positions so it clears the turret's rotation footprint at rest pose. Now I'm starting on the cab details, beginning with the head area.

Then front headlights, a dark bumper box with a hazard decal, and a winch; side windows get glass-textured planes sized to the cab width. I'm reconsidering side skirts since they'd overlap the wheel positions, so I'm skipping those and instead planning a unit number decal plane on the chassis side, working around the wheel placement.

I'm now mapping wheel gaps along the chassis to find a clear spot, then shifting to the turret: putting an emblem on the turret side, but the capacitor cylinders at x 1.3 would block it, so I'm testing roof placement for the cylinders instead, checking against the roof rail and breech geometry for conflicts before settling on a lower side position at x ±1.25, y 2.2.

Now I'm placing the unit stencil text on the lower hull rear and cab door, with the emblem positioned near the turret front, then moving to the radar mast — positioning a lathe-profile dish on the cab roof at x 0.85 to avoid the rail, and working out the dish's cross-section outline points.

Next I'm adding whip antennas rising from the generator rear with glowing red tips, exhaust stacks as small cylinders on the generator top, and starting on the six wheels with tire geometry using a 12-sided cylinder for the tread.

Still writing tread blocks...

That's within tolerance of the floor, so I'll set the tire center height to .7 and adjust the chassis to sit higher at center 1.45 with height .9, making sure the fenders clear the wheel tops with a small margin — though I notice the chassis bottom at 1.0 may still overlap the wheels, so I need to recheck that gap.

Checking wheel positions against chassis width confirms clearance at the corners, so I'm raising the chassis top to 1.9 and setting the cab and turret ring base there too, with the cab profile extending up to 3.05. For the arms connecting to the legs, I'm positioning them between the wheels at z 1.4 with enough width to avoid collision, and now I'm working out the axle rod placement under the chassis along with the differential bulge.

Now I'm placing a low-poly sphere for the differential, deciding to skip suspension arms but adding leaf spring boxes from axle to chassis, and designing the wheel hub as a steel cylinder with a textured outer face showing lug nuts, sizing and positioning it to align flush with the tire's outer edge.

Now I'm adding hull surface details -- side belt panels, orange stripes, hazard planes on the bumper, and figuring out where to fit side tool boxes between the wheel gaps by calculating the open space along the z-axis between the front and rear wheel positions.

I'll also place access ladders near the rear legs and start planning procedurally generated textures: a hazard stripe pattern, a circular emblem with wings, and a stenciled identification text texture for the hull markings.

Adding more textures...

Working through the camera orientation math, I confirm that both the left and right side text panels read correctly in natural vehicle-reading direction, with front-to-rear orientation matching normal conventions on each side. Now I'm setting up the lathe operation to create the dish shape along the given axis.

Positioning the turret and cab extrusions on the hull, tuning their base heights, thickness, and bevel values, and confirming the panelled paint grid uses the dominant axis correctly. I'm also sizing the glow strip between the rails to fit within the rail inner edges and assigning it a cyan glow color.

Now I'm placing the gun cylinder and its mounting supports on the turret roof, working out roof height from the turret profile coordinates, adjusting the pivot point upward to clear the rails, and checking cab clearance against the tilted roof angle.

I'm checking the breech block position near the rear of the turret — it sinks slightly into the roof but that's fine since it's hidden within the turret mass. Now moving on to write the cylinder helper code for the wing geometry.

Still writing leg code...

Placing the rear outriggers and generator housing now, with vent panels on the rear and side faces of the gen box, plus exhaust stacks and a rear light fixture.

For the cab I'm adding window planes, a front vent under the windscreen, glowing headlight boxes embedded in the front chassis face, and a bumper block centered below.

I'm placing hazard light planes on the bumper's front face, an orange glow beacon cylinder on the roof, and sketching out angled side armor plates plus rows of smoke launcher tubes on the turret's front corners.

Now I'm working out positions for the emblem decal and stencil text on the turret's side, along with capacitor cylinders beneath them, checking the vertical spacing so everything stacks cleanly above the turret base without overlapping.

Positioning three small cylindrical tubes along the z-axis near the rear, then shifting to hatches on the turret roof — placing a cylinder hatch centered around y 3.07, checking it doesn't collide with the rail rings or breech positions at x ±0.55-0.9.

Adding a camera mast rod on the roof, confirming shading and triangle counts stay reasonable, then setting up helper functions for positioning: a pitch-rotated direction vector, an R(t,x,y) offset helper, and a gbox function to place boxes along that oriented axis for building the final code sheet under 40 lines.

I'm checking the glow wrapper works on parts with meshes, and merging wheel tread geometries with BufferGeometryUtils into a single indexed mesh without bones since no joints are needed, while considering flat shading for the tire cylinders.
